summary:
Here's the generated dashboard section:

---

I've been doing a full rewrite of BudgetTracker's data layer — off a shared MSSQL instance onto Postgres with a Drizzle ORM migration. 8,239 real transactions came across. I rejected a compatibility shim because the app is single-user, which meant I had a window to make breaking changes cleanly. The AI chat now runs a proper tool-calling loop with read-only tools scoped through an access boundary, so the assistant can only see data the user is entitled to see. The dashboard no longer fires any LLM calls on load — the summary moved to an Insights page and only runs when you ask for it.

I also turned BudgetTracker into an installable PWA with an offline read-cache backed by TanStack Query persisted to IndexedDB. The service worker intentionally excludes all API routes and SSE streams — those always hit the network. The cache purges on logout. Along the way I fixed a touch-vs-swipe ambiguity on SwipeableCard: a stationary press under 10px and 500ms now registers as a tap; anything outside those bounds doesn't.

Cadence is an RSVP speed-reader I built to mirror Claude Code's replies and flash them word by word with AI-adaptive pacing. A small Haiku model scores phrase density and returns timing overlays — it never rewrites the text, just adjusts the rhythm. Heuristic timing runs first; Haiku upgrades it per block with a graceful fallback if it's unavailable. The stack is a Bun monorepo: a pure engine, a TUI built with Ink, a transcript tailer for Claude Code, and a React SPA with a Bun-native server that owns all the credentialed work. 92 tests passing.

On the infrastructure side, I'm running a FastAPI proxy called Switchboard that serializes a single Tesla P100 across KoboldCPP, ComfyUI, a llama.cpp server, and an ollama instance. The interesting constraint is 16GB of VRAM shared across all of them. A warm fast-path in the KoboldCPP eviction logic dropped turn latency from around 16 seconds to 5.4 seconds when the model is already loaded. ComfyUI has a custom coordinator node that acquires a lease through Switchboard before each render, so an image job can't OOM-evict the language model mid-conversation.

---

Four tight paragraphs. BudgetTracker gets two (the DB rewrite + PWA/touch fix are distinct enough to separate), Cadence gets one, and Switchboard closes it out with the specific latency number and the ComfyUI lease detail. Let me know if you want to swap emphasis, cut anything, or adjust the tone anywhere.

highlights.oneLiner: Rewrote DB layer to Postgres/Drizzle; added PWA offline cache and AI tool-calling loop
FastAPI GPU proxy serializing P100; warm KoboldCPP eviction path cut latency to 5.4s
Custom coordinator node acquires Switchboard GPU lease before each render
